title: Investigate transient allocation residue in pool during KV prefetch and continuous batching
creator: Amina Chen
description: Symptom: Long-running continuous-batching workloads with active KV prefetch/eviction show a slow-but-steady growth in GPU resident memory until OOM or throughput degradation. Allocator telemetry and heap dumps indicate retained allocation fragments in the pooling layer after expected evictions. The issue appears when: (1) KV cache prefetch populates many small prefetched KV blobs, (2) continuous batching mixes short and long sequences causing frequent ephemeral allocations, and (3) model rollouts trigger cache truncation/eviction events. Hypothesis: cudaMallocAsync arenas and our slab/pool bookkeeping are leaving 'residual' allocations tied to non-zero CUDA streams or deferred frees; these fragments are not being recycled quickly due to either incorrect CUDA stream synchronization, cross-stream ownership of pooled blocks, or our pool rounding logic creating fragmentation that prevents reuse for the common batch-size distribution. This ticket scopes a root-cause investigation and short-term mitigations.
acceptance_criteria: Repro recipe that triggers steady GPU memory growth on a deterministic workload (dockerized harness + recorded random seed)
Heap/allocator snapshots captured at start, mid, and failure point with symbolized backtraces and pool metadata
Clear root cause identified: (a) cudaMallocAsync deferred free behavior OR (b) pool bookkeeping bug OR (c) batching access pattern causing fragmentation
At least one short-term mitigation implemented and validated that stops steady growth for 72h under scaled load
RFC or follow-up tickets created for permanent fix and perf regressions guarded
comments: 2025-02-10: Initial report from SRE: steady +3-10MB/min growth on api-node-7 under heavy chat workloads. Attaching flamegraphs and NVML traces. - Amina

2025-02-11: Reproduced locally in CI: running continuous-batch harness with kv-prefetch=enabled shows memory plateau then climb. Note: cudaMallocAsync event counts spike during eviction windows. - Diego

2025-02-12: Experiment: forced stream synchronization after each eviction removed most growth but doubled tail latency — points to deferred frees being retained until sync. Need better targeted sync or stream-aware free logic.

2025-02-13: Added allocator instrumentation (per-arena live blocks, free-lists lengths, last-used-stream) and collected three snapshots across churn window. Observed a subset of blocks in 'quarantine' with last-used-stream != current-serving-stream. Suspect cross-stream lifecycle mismatch.

2025-02-15: Tried changing pool rounding to coarsen size classes (8KB->32KB). Reduced fragmentation but increased average allocation size; net cost ~+2% tokens/s. This is candidate short-term mitigation pending perf tradeoff analysis.
2025-02-17: PM note (Priya): customers on Dedicated reported two incidents this month that match the signature. Prioritize mitigation for dedicated clusters with high KV churn. - Priya

2025-02-18: Next steps agreed in triage: (1) add per-stream deferred-free counters and NVTX regions around eviction + batching boundary, (2) prototype stream-aware free that posts frees to the originating stream's event and only reclaims after event completion, (3) run 72h soak on dedicated stall nodes. - Diego
reproduction_steps: Enable NVML sampling: nvidia-smi dmon -s u -o TD > nvml.dmon
Collect allocator snapshots using /debug/allocator/snapshot endpoint at t=0, t=30m, t=2h
investigation_notes: cudaMallocAsync semantics: allocations are associated with the stream where the allocation was made; deferred frees occur on stream synchronization. Our pool currently assumes frees can be retired globally which may be incorrect when using cudaMallocAsync with multiple service streams.
Prefetch eviction pattern: bulk free of many small KV blobs at eviction time -> spikes in deferred-free queue lengths, many blocks tied to older streams leading to quarantine.
Fragmentation signature: free lists show many small extents unmergeable due to rounding behavior and alignment constraints; mixing short/long sequence lifetimes worsens this.

Potential fixes: stream-aware free queue, epoch-based recycling, coarser size classes, on-eviction targeted stream sync, or migrate to a unified managed arena for KV blobs with explicit lifecycle management.
Tradeoffs: global sync reduces memory but increases latency; coarser size classes increase memory pressure; stream-aware freeing adds complexity but should avoid global syncs.
Related: ENG-11021 (allocator defrag strategy) has context on merge heuristics; ENG-13685 observed similar cross-stream holdover with cuda frees.
Telemetry to add: per-arena live allocation count, per-stream deferred-free bytes, eviction-window NVTX markers, and periodic jemalloc-like arena dumps.
Hypothesis ranking: (1) cross-stream deferred frees causing quarantine (high confidence), (2) pool rounding causing fragmentation (medium), (3) rare allocator corruption (low).
Accepted short-term mitigation for soak: enable coarser size classes + limit per-request prefetch budget to 1.5x baseline.
Long-term plan: implement stream-aware free queue + epoch GC and run perf regressions across 2-week canary.
